cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Consequences Compound
cards.instruction: Make each new choice carry a larger reward, cost, audience, or point of no return.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've signed below you. Our table-tennis game decides who cleans up tonight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I signed for a borrowed bat. That's the equipment book.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, putting commitments in writing. Loser cleans for the whole month; enter that beside the bats.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm returning mine at six, when the club meets. I haven't agreed to your bet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll settle the terms at six in front of the club. If you agree there, everyone gets to hold us to the month.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies a signature as a wager; B2 exposes equipment borrowing and A3 claims written commitments while expanding the cost; A5 adds the public enforcement available in B4.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 equipment book becomes A3 wager record; B4 six-o'clock club meeting becomes A5 audience and accountability.

relationship.evidence: B4 refuses the wager and has an independent reason to attend the meeting.

heightening.evidence: A5 increases the audience and durability of the choice because B4 names an actual gathering.

specificity.evidence: A1 table tennis/cleanup and B2 bat book make the error clear; B4 explains time and audience.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 conditional if you agree preserves B's actual refusal and avoids inventing consent.
